title: Linear systems of ODEs
lead: A system of linear ODEs is written in the language of matrices and vectors. This section sets up that language: vector-valued and matrix-valued functions and their derivatives, the first-order linear system $\kvecxprime = \kP\kvecx + \kvecf$, how solutions of a homogeneous system combine, the fundamental matrix they form, and how an initial condition picks out one solution.
notes: The section notes (the lecture count and the [EP] and [BD] section numbers) are left out.
exercise_notes: Bloom levels and concept tags are AI-generated. Exercises 3.3.101–3.3.104 carry the book’s own answers. Exercises 3.3.1–3.3.6, which the book leaves unanswered, carry AI-marked solutions stating the answer and the reasoning, every computed value checked with SymPy first.

exercises.prompt: Write the system $\kxoneprime = 2 \kxone - 3t \kxtwo + \sin t$, $\kxtwoprime = e^t \kxone + 3 \kxtwo + \cos t$ in the form $\kvecxprime = \kP(t) \kvecx + \kvecf(t)$.

answer.solution: $\kvecxprime = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3t \\ e^t & 3 \end{bmatrix} \kvecx + \begin{bmatrix} \sin t \\ \cos t \end{bmatrix}$, so $\kP(t) = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3t \\ e^t & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\kvecf(t) = \begin{bmatrix} \sin t \\ \cos t \end{bmatrix}$. Each row of $\kP(t)$ holds the coefficients of $\kxone$ and $\kxtwo$ in one equation, and the terms with neither go into $\kvecf(t)$. Multiplying out, the first row gives $2\kxone - 3t\kxtwo + \sin t$ and the second $e^t\kxone + 3\kxtwo + \cos t$, the two right-hand sides.

exercises.prompt:
1. Verify that the system $\kvecxprime = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] \kvecx$ has the two solutions $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] e^{4t}$ and $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] e^{-2t}$.
  2. Write down the general solution.
  3. Write down the general solution in the form $\kxone = ?$, $\kxtwo = ?$ (i.e. write down a formula for each element of the solution).

answer.solution: a) $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} = 4\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$, so for $\kvecx = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{4t}$ both $\kvecxprime$ and $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\kvecx$ equal $\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}e^{4t}$. Likewise $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} = -2\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$, so for $\kvecx = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t}$ both sides equal $\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t}$. b) The two solutions are linearly independent (at $t = 0$ they are $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}$, neither a multiple of the other) and the system has two equations, so by superposition (Theorem 3.3.1) every solution is $\kvecx = c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{4t} + c_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}e^{-2t}$. c) $\kxone = c_1 e^{4t} + c_2 e^{-2t}$, $\kxtwo = c_1 e^{4t} - c_2 e^{-2t}$.

exercises.prompt: Verify that $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] e^{t}$ and $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] e^{t}$ are linearly independent. Hint: Just plug in $t=0$.

answer.solution: Suppose $c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{t} + c_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}e^{t} = \vec{0}$ for all $t$. At $t = 0$ this reads $c_1 + c_2 = 0$ and $c_1 - c_2 = 0$; adding the two gives $2c_1 = 0$, so $c_1 = 0$ and then $c_2 = 0$. Only the zero combination works, so the two functions are linearly independent.

exercises.prompt: Verify that $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{smallmatrix} \right] e^{t}$ and $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] e^{t}$ and $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix} \right] e^{2t}$ are linearly independent. Hint: You must be a bit more tricky than in the previous exercise.

answer.solution: Suppose $c_1 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}e^{t} + c_2 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{t} + c_3 \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}e^{2t} = \vec{0}$ for all $t$. Plugging in $t = 0$ alone is not enough, since the last two vectors are then equal. The third entry says $c_2 e^{t} + c_3 e^{2t} = 0$ for all $t$; dividing by $e^{t}$, $c_2 + c_3 e^{t} = 0$, which at $t = 0$ and $t = 1$ gives $c_2 + c_3 = 0$ and $c_2 + c_3 e = 0$. Subtracting, $c_3(e - 1) = 0$, so $c_3 = 0$ and $c_2 = 0$. The first entry is then $c_1 e^{t} = 0$, so $c_1 = 0$. Only the zero combination works: the three functions are linearly independent.

exercises.prompt: Verify that $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} t \\ t^2 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$ and $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} t^3 \\ t^4 \end{smallmatrix} \right]$ are linearly independent.

answer.solution: Suppose $c_1 \begin{bmatrix} t \\ t^2 \end{bmatrix} + c_2 \begin{bmatrix} t^3 \\ t^4 \end{bmatrix} = \vec{0}$ for all $t$. Plugging in $t = 0$ gives nothing, since both functions vanish there. The first entry says $c_1 t + c_2 t^3 = 0$ for all $t$: at $t = 1$ this is $c_1 + c_2 = 0$, and at $t = 2$ it is $2c_1 + 8c_2 = 0$. Putting $c_1 = -c_2$ into the second, $6c_2 = 0$, so $c_2 = 0$ and $c_1 = 0$. Only the zero combination works, so the two functions are linearly independent.

exercises.prompt:
Take the system $\kxoneprime + \kxtwoprime = \kxone$, $\kxoneprime - \kxtwoprime = \kxtwo$.

  1. Write it in the form $\kA \kvecxprime = \kB \kvecx$ for matrices $\kA$ and $\kB$.
  2. Compute $\kA^{-1}$ and use that to write the system in the form $\kvecxprime = \kP \kvecx$.

answer.solution: a) The left-hand sides are $\begin{bmatrix} \kxoneprime + \kxtwoprime \\ \kxoneprime - \kxtwoprime \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \kvecxprime$ and the right-hand sides are $\begin{bmatrix} \kxone \\ \kxtwo \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \kvecx$, so $\kA = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $\kB = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = I$. b) $\det \kA = (1)(-1) - (1)(1) = -2$, so $\kA^{-1} = \frac{1}{-2}\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1/2 & 1/2 \\ 1/2 & -1/2 \end{bmatrix}$. Multiplying $\kA \kvecxprime = \kB \kvecx$ on the left by $\kA^{-1}$ gives $\kvecxprime = \kA^{-1}\kB\kvecx$, so $\kP = \kA^{-1}\kB = \kA^{-1}$ and $\kvecxprime = \begin{bmatrix} 1/2 & 1/2 \\ 1/2 & -1/2 \end{bmatrix} \kvecx$; that is, $\kxoneprime = \frac{\kxone + \kxtwo}{2}$ and $\kxtwoprime = \frac{\kxone - \kxtwo}{2}$, whose sum and difference give back the original two equations.

exercises.prompt: Are $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} e^{2t} \\ e^t \end{smallmatrix}\right]$ and $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} e^{t} \\ e^{2t} \end{smallmatrix}\right]$ linearly independent? Justify.

Are $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} \cosh(t) \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right]$, $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} e^{t} \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right]$, and $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} e^{-t} \\ 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right]$ linearly independent? Justify.

answer.solution: $\left[ \begin{smallmatrix} x \\ y \end{smallmatrix}\right] ' = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ t & 0 \end{smallmatrix}\right] \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} x \\ y \end{smallmatrix}\right] + \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} e^{t} \\ 0 \end{smallmatrix}\right]$

exercises.prompt:
1. Write $\kxoneprime=2t\kxtwo$, $\kxtwoprime=2t\kxtwo$ in matrix notation.
  2. Solve and write the solution in matrix notation.

answer.solution: a) $\kvecxprime = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} 0 & 2t \\ 0 & 2t \end{smallmatrix}\right] \kvecx$ b) $\kvecx = \left[ \begin{smallmatrix} C_2 e^{t^2} + C_1 \\ C_2 e^{t^2} \end{smallmatrix}\right]$
